nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show diffraction peak at 38.6° ascribed to Ni(OH)₂ (PDF #14-0117) and peaks at 28.4°, 33.1°, 56.7° assigned to CeO₂ (PDF #34-0394) in S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF (Figure 1b) shows that the diffraction peak at 38.6° is ascribed to Ni(OH)₂ (PDF #14-0117), and the peaks at 28.4°, 33.1°, and 56.7° are assigned to CeO₂ (PDF #34-0394)

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Ni 2p spectra of Ni(OH)₂/NF, S-Ni(OH)₂/NF, and S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF show Ni 2p₃/₂ peak ~855 eV indicating Ni²⁺; S-Ni(OH)₂/NF shifts +0.3 eV (electron transfer from Ni due to S-doping); S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF shifts -0.5 eV (electron transfer to Ni due to CeO₂).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p₃/₂ peak of S-Ni(OH)₂/NF shows a positive shift towards the higher binding energy by 0.3 eV compared with that of Ni(OH)₂/NF, suggesting the electron transfer from Ni to adjacent atoms due to S-doping. The peak of Ni in S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF presents an opposite variation with a 0.5 eV negative shift upon the incorporation of CeO₂

nodes.characterization_summary: S 2p spectrum of S-Ni(OH)₂/NF shows peaks at 168.7 eV (sulfate) and 163.1 eV (S²⁻); S²⁻ peak in S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF shifts 0.8 eV lower.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution S 2p spectrum of S-Ni(OH)₂/NF (Figure 1d) displays that there are two peaks centered at 168.7 and 163.1 eV corresponding to sulfate and S²⁻, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce 3d spectrum of S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF shows peaks for Ce³⁺ (u₀, u') and Ce⁴⁺ (u, u'', u''') indicating mixed valence states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ce 3d spectrum of S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF (Figure 1e) can be deconvoluted into several peaks marked as u₀, u, u', u'', and u''' assigning to Ce 3d₃/₂ while the v''' belong to Ce 3d₅/₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Ni(OH)₂/NF with uniform nanoplates, S-Ni(OH)₂/NF with oblique nanosheets, and S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF with vertical nanorod arrays.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphological structures of Ni(OH)₂/NF, S-Ni(OH)₂/NF, and S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF electrodes were explored by scanning electron microscope (SEM) measurements as shown in Figure 2.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows nanorods of 2.5 μm length, 0.5 μm diameter; lattice spacings 0.23 nm for Ni(OH)₂ (011), 0.19 nm (220), 0.16 nm (311), 0.27 nm (200) for CeO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3a, the length and diameter of the nanorods are 2.5 and 0.5 μm, respectively. As presented in Figure 3b,c, the lattice spacing of ≈0.23 nm for the areas ① can be attributed to the (011) plane of Ni(OH)₂

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image and corresponding EDS elemental mappings confirm presence and distribution of Ni, Ce, O, S elements; Ce aggregates while Ni and S are uniformly dispersed, indicating S-doping into Ni(OH)₂ and hybrid S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂ nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) (Figure 3d) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images (Figure 3e-i) demonstrate that the existence of Ni, Ce, O, and S in the sample. Especially... the Ce element (Figure 3f) aggregates in these areas while the Ni (Figure 3e) and S elements (Figure 3h) are dispersed uniformly

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitances calculated as 4.95 mF cm⁻² for Ni(OH)₂/NF, 7.33 mF cm⁻² for S-Ni(OH)₂/NF, 9.26 mF cm⁻² for S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF; ECSAs 123.7, 183.2, 231.5 cm² respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The double-layer capacitances (Cdl) of Ni(OH)₂/NF, S-Ni(OH)₂/NF, and S-Ni(OH)₂/CeO₂/NF were calculated from their cyclic voltammetry (CV) plots... and estimated to be 4.95, 7.33, and 9.26 mF cm⁻², respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform Ni and S distribution with Ce aggregation, verifying S-doping into Ni(OH)₂ and CeO₂ interfacing in the hybrid nanorod structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) (Figure 3d) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images (Figure 3e-i) demonstrate that the existence of Ni, Ce, O, and S in the sample.
